sources.name: Basis for determining Q347
sources.note: The low-flow reference the Water Protection Act runs on. Its age is not simply a defect: Art. 4(h) defines Q347 as a ten-year average, and the decade the cantons worked from is the one in this file. It is the legally operative figure and an obsolete description of the river at the same time.

sources.name: Residual-flow map: the cantonal inventory of existing abstractions
sources.note: The inventory the cantons filed under GSchG Art. 80 ff. A licence granted, changed or restored since the data state is not in it. It carries no volume.

sources.name: Treatment plants and their share of the receiving water at Q347
sources.note: From a survey of 2011, taken before the fourth treatment stage was built out. Every plant upgraded since is described here as it was before the upgrade.

sources.name: Groundwater bodies
sources.licence: FSDI general terms of use, free use with source attribution
sources.note: Drawn as a WMS image, not held as data. The page cannot query it, cannot check it, and reads its date from the same legend endpoint as every other federal layer.

sources.name: River network, catchment area and long-term mean discharge
sources.licence: Free for non-commercial and commercial use with attribution
sources.note: Traced from a 15 arc-second grid, so its lines carry the staircase of the raster. The long-term mean it carries is a model output, not a gauge reading.

sources.name: Nuclear power stations
sources.note: The clearest case of a register outliving its subject: it still carries Mühleberg as a power station, and its data state is the day Mühleberg was shut down. The page corrects it and shows the correction, rather than quietly dropping the site.

sources.name: Lakes and the national border
sources.note: Carries no reading. It is there so the water has a country to sit in.

sources.name: Drinking-water protection zones S1 to S3, in force (oldest delivery: NE)
sources.licence: per canton; all 26 currently publish this model freely
sources.note: There is no federal layer. This is 26 cantonal deliveries of the minimal geodata model Planerischer Gewaesserschutz aggregated into one service, so it has no single data state: the date given is the OLDEST cantonal delivery, because that is how old the picture actually is.

sources.name: Swiss Glacier Inventory 1850 and 2023, and glacier length change
sources.cadence: the inventories are episodic; lengths annual
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 per the DOI index; the length-change file header adds "scientific and non-commercial use". Both statements stand.
sources.note: doi:10.18750/inventory.sgi1850.r1992, doi:10.18750/inventory.sgi2023.r2026, doi:10.18750/lengthchange.2025.r2025. The 2023 inventory was released in 2026 but describes the ice as it stood at the end of the 2023 melt season, and that is the date given here: what a source describes, not when it was published.

sources.name: Dams under federal supervision
sources.note: Structures, with the volume each reservoir holds when full. It carries no fill state, and never has.

sources.name: Sub-catchments of Switzerland, 2 km2
sources.licence: FSDI general terms of use, free use with source attribution
sources.note: Drawn as a WMS image. Which ground drains to which water; it carries no quantity.

sources.name: Statistics of hydropower plants from 300 kW up (WASTA)
sources.note: The freshest of the registers. It carries capacity and head but no water quantity, so the discharge on the map is derived by arithmetic.

sources.name: Names of the watercourses, lakes, glaciers and springs
sources.licence: Open data, free use with source attribution
sources.note: A gazetteer of name placements, not of named geometries. Each anchor is joined to the nearest drawn reach, which is what gives a name its rank and its angle. The join fails predictably where a canal runs within 200 m of a trunk river: build/10-names.mjs names the cases it gets wrong rather than hiding them.

sources.name: Filling level of the storage reservoirs, weekly, in GWh
sources.note: The file allows only map.geo.admin.ch to read it from a browser, so it is baked in at build time. The Pages workflow rebuilds weekly to keep the baked copy fresh.

sources.name: Discharge, water level and temperature at the federal gauges
sources.note: The only live source on the page. Its age is the age of the last reading, shown in the title bar.

sources.name: Relief shading and the grey national map, optional ground
sources.licence: FSDI general terms of use, free use with source attribution
sources.note: Both are off unless asked for and neither carries a reading. They are here so a site can be found on the ground, not so anything can be measured from them.
